title: Mark Zuckerberg's Superyacht Draws Boos in Seattle as Meta Layoffs Hit
text:
Mark Zuckerberg's $300 million superyacht, named Launchpad, drew boos and heckles as it docked in Seattle's Ballard neighborhood on the same day that Meta announced layoffs in the area. The boat's appearance was met with loud condemnation on social media, with some people accusing Zuckerberg of being 'just another tech bro who can't read the room.' The layoffs at Meta were part of a nationwide bloodbath, with potential cuts affecting over 15,000 employees. Investors reacted positively to Meta's stock rise, but the company's push to improve efficiency through AI tools has also led to layoffs.
Mark Zuckerberg has rubbed salt into the wounds of hundreds of Meta employees who were recently laid off in Seattle by parking his superyacht in the city's harbor.
The tech tycoon's $300 million vessel pulled up on Tuesday, casting a shadow over the metro area where 1,400 workers had just been made redundant. Named the 'Launchpad', the boat was reportedly met with a round of boos and heckles as it docked beside Seattle's Ballard neighborhood. Zuckerberg did not appear to be on board the yacht. One heckler shouted at the boat to 'pay some f***ing taxes', according to GeekWire.
The boat's appearance was also loudly condemned by people on social media, as one person berated Zuckerberg as 'just another tech bro who can't read the room.
' 'Zuck’s boat arrives to Seattle the day that Meta cuts their workforce by 20 percent in area. Can’t make this up,' another person wrote on X. The local cuts were part of a nationwide bloodbath which has seen Meta threaten to cut more than 20 percent of its workforce as it pours billions into AI instead. Potential cuts could affect over 15,000 of the tech giant's employees, according to sources cited by Reuters.
The redundancies at Meta came as Zuckerberg poured vast sums into new data centers, research teams, and powerful AI models. Meta has 31 data centers across the globe, with server space to process and store the billions of messages, posts, and images circulated on Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp every single second of the day. In June 2025, the company invested $14.3 billion in Scale AI, a software company that was poached by Meta along with its CEO Alexandr Wang.
Despite reports of planned layoffs from Reuters, the company’s push to improve efficiency through its AI tools appears to be paying off. Investors reacted positively, with Meta’s stock rising three percent to 632 in early trading this morning. Meta is not alone in linking artificial intelligence to layoffs. Amazon cut around 16,000 jobs in January as it restructures while investing heavily in AI.
It marked the second major round of layoffs in just three months after slashing 14,000 roles in October. Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey is cutting half the jobs at his payments firm, Block, as it shifts toward smaller teams powered by automation. Software company Atlassian also announced plans to cut about 10 percent of its workforce to focus on AI.
Across the US, more than 12,000 layoffs this year have already been tied directly to artificial intelligence, according to consulting firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas
